hyps.why: Parallel conv3x3 paths into the output are redundant, so the marginal gain shrinks.
A conv3x3 on edge 5 already supplies strong capacity into the output, so the marginal gain of edge 3 shrinks.
Removing edge 1 costs nothing when edge 5 already cuts node 2 off from the output, whereas otherwise it costs accuracy.
With edge 4 absent, removing the direct edge leaves fewer routes to the output and costs more.
With the direct edge absent, removing edge 5 strips a main remaining route to the output.
With the direct edge absent, removing edge 4 strips a main remaining route to the output.
Any parameter-free op replacing none restores the direct path, a larger gain than replacing a real op.
With edge 4 absent, edge 0 reaches the output only via edges 2 and 5, limiting its contribution.
Upgrading conv1x1 to conv3x3 is a small gain compared with the large gains from upgrading none or pooling.
Skip is already a strong op on the direct edge, so the upgrade to conv3x3 gains less.
